question: Should OpenClaw adopt indefinite pending retention for ambiguous outbound deliveries when no reconciliation-capable adapter exists?
rationale: Both available automatic outcomes have user-visible costs: terminalizing can permanently lose a future reconciliation opportunity, while indefinite pending retention can strand messages and accumulate unresolved state. Repository policy treats fallback and delivery compatibility as owner decisions.

options.title: Accept Pending-First Recovery
options.body: Merge the current policy so no-reconciler ambiguous rows remain recoverable without blind replay or retry-budget consumption, with visibility and adapter reconciliation handled as follow-up work.

options.title: Require Bounded Escalation
options.body: Add a documented age or operator-action boundary that preserves duplicate safety while eventually surfacing or terminalizing unresolved rows.

options.title: Pause For Full Reconciliation
options.body: Hold this mitigation until the canonical receipt-ledger and adapter reconciliation design can resolve unknown sends rather than merely retaining them.

recommendation.title: Accept Pending-First Recovery
recommendation.body: Merge the current policy so no-reconciler ambiguous rows remain recoverable without blind replay or retry-budget consumption, with visibility and adapter reconciliation handled as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows ownership of the shared outbound recovery and replay-safety boundary that this policy changes.
